summary: Mobayi-Mbongo territory (Nord-Ubangi) lies on the Ubangi river border with the Central African Republic, opposite Mobaye, far from the eastern conflict zones. No Congolese or foreign armed group is reported to hold territory; the territorial seat (Mobayi-Mbongo/Ziamba Sango) and surrounding villages fall under PNC posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs, with FARDC and border services deployed along the river. The Kotakoli area hosts a long-standing FARDC military base/training centre, where the army is the main permanent force. Insecurity consists of ordinary crime and periodic spill-over concerns from CAR (refugee inflows, cross-border armed elements, e.g. after fighting around Mobaye) that do not amount to territorial control. Web search was unavailable in this run (search budget exhausted and search engines blocked), so the assessment rests on default state presence and general knowledge.

zones.description: Mobayi-Mbongo territorial seat (Ziamba Sango, Mando, Zuanguba) and nearby villages in Mobayi, Bassa, Mbui and Nyaki health areas along the Ubangi river
zones.evidence: Territorial seat with territorial administration, PNC commissariat and border/river services facing Mobaye (CAR); FARDC units deployed along the border. No reported armed-group presence or parallel authority; CAR spill-over has been limited to refugees and occasional cross-border incidents.

zones.description: Kotakoli area (Boboto, Gido, Polongo Yangamo; Kotakoli 1 and 2 health areas) around the FARDC Kotakoli military base
zones.evidence: Kotakoli hosts a long-standing FARDC military base and training centre, making the army the main permanent armed force in the settlements around it; no armed-group activity reported. Not verified with recent sources in this run.

zones.description: Rural villages elsewhere in the territory (Inke, Nwenenge, Gbadogboketsa, Maniko, Fulu, Simbala, Sowa, Zamba, Vote, Sokoro health areas, and Loko/Bowozo and Fiwa areas)
zones.evidence: Rural villages with no reported armed-group activity; PNC posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs are the default authority, with FARDC deployed along the CAR border. No recent sources could be retrieved in this run.
